subject: Life Skills
title: Too Good To Be True
description: A micro-lesson that makes Too Good To Be True usable.

hook.text: Free iPhone, just pay shipping. 10x investment returns guaranteed. You won a prize you never entered. Same pattern.

buildup.text: Scams exploit two emotions: greed and fear. 'Too good to be true' targets greed. 'Act now or lose' targets fear.

discovery.text: Legitimate offers do not need urgency or secrecy. If you are told not to tell anyone, that is confirmation it is a scam.

twist.text: Sophisticated scams use small real payouts early to build trust. Then the big ask comes once you are committed.

climax.text: Before accepting any unsolicited offer, search the exact phrasing online.

punchline.text: If it sounds too good, someone is paying. It is you.

quiz.question: Why do some scams offer small real payouts at first?
options: To prove they are legitimate businesses
To build trust before making a larger fraudulent ask
Because small transactions are harder to trace
